source: Mokhatab et al. (2014) Handbook of Liquefied Natural Gas, Elsevier (ch. 9 send-out & vaporization); Pospíšil et al. (2019) Renewable & Sustainable Energy Reviews 99, 1-15 (LNG cold-energy utilization); Egashira (2013) Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Tech. Rev. 50(1) (ORV/SCV).

vaporizer.name: Open-Rack Vaporizer (ORV) seawater-heated, generic onshore terminal

type.note: ORV=open-rack seawater, SCV=submerged combustion, AAV=ambient air

UA.note: Overall conductance heat-source side -> vaporizer metal. ORV seawater UA is large (panel arrays); sized so a 500 t/h ORV transfers ~100 MW at ~25 K LMTD.

UA_process.note: Conductance vaporizer metal -> LNG/gas process stream.

m_metal.note: Lumped thermal mass of vaporizer panels/tubes (aluminium ORV racks).

cp_metal.note: Specific heat of aluminium vaporizer structure.

T_heat_source.note: Seawater supply temperature (15 C). For SCV this is the hot flue-gas/water-bath temperature.

eta_combustion.note: Fuel-gas fraction burned for SCV self-heating (0 for seawater ORV; ~0.015-0.02 of throughput LHV for SCV).

P_discharge.note: HP pump send-out pressure (~80 bar pipeline).

P_tank.note: LNG storage tank pressure (~1.15 bar abs).

h_fg.note: Latent heat of vaporization of methane at 1 atm boiling point (Younglove & Ely 1987, NIST).

cp_liquid.note: Liquid methane specific heat near boiling point (NIST/Younglove 1987).

cp_gas.note: Methane gas cp at near-ambient send-out conditions (NIST, ~2.2 kJ/kg.K).

T_storage.note: LNG saturated storage temperature (-162 C) at 1 atm.
